comments.author: @tlw1842
comments.text: I have owned an EV for over three years now, and I have gone exclusively EV for over a year now. I have a 2023 Tesla Model Y Long Range and a 2025 GMC Hummer EV SUV. I charge at home, and sometimes out in the wild when needed. I have personally taken the Tesla on a trip across the country with absolutely zero issues. I live in western Washington where EVs are more popular than other parts of the country, but maybe not like California. After all of my experiences, I can honestly say that I can't relate to anything in this video at all. My experience has been tremendous in both of my vehicles. Charging anywhere has been seamless, on and off the Tesla network. Even at home without a Tesla charger. As long as you are responsible with maintaining your charge level and not letting it go down to nearly dead (like less than 5%), it is not really an issue. Granted, I see the issues with many other EVs that I wouldn't buy, like the Mini, Fiat, Mustang, F150 Lightning, Challenger, and Mercedes and Audi products. However, given the decent products out there from like Hyundai, Kia, Tesla, and GMC, it is legitmately possible to live everyday life with these and be ok. I would say that you should own or rent your own house and not be in an apartment complex before considering these purchases first right now though. Makes the wait on charging go from 30 minutes to an hour a week or two to basically zero.
